tools.name: apply_composition
tools.title: Apply Composition
tools.description: Atomically apply an array of CompositionOps to a project composition. All ops succeed or none do (transactional). Call describe_composition_ops without type for the compact operation list, then with a type for its exact JSON Schema. For negotiated component execution, read get_composition with componentExecutionVersions=["3","4"] and includeDependencies="true", then send componentExecutionVersions:[3,4] and that exact expectedBrandIdentity. A changed brand refuses the command; never refresh the witness to conceal a conflict. Explicit builtinSources selectors attach only the approved exact source pins referenced by the final composition. The additive `concurrency` envelope requires an endpoint confirmed to enforce guardedCompositionV1; unsupported hosted endpoints refuse it with unsupported_concurrency. Obtain dependency expectations from the observed composition; never rebuild a stale basis from current state. Every committing call REQUIRES `if_match`, the composition ETag from a fresh get_composition, or the `concurrency` envelope; a call with neither is refused with 428 precondition_required. On 409 stale_etag, read get_composition again and reconsider the batch against what changed; never copy the error's currentEtag into a retry without that read. `dry_run: true` validates the batch without persisting and needs no revision. Ops land on the project's ACTIVE composition unless you pass `composition_id` (mutually exclusive with `session_id`), which targets a specific one — that is how you author a second composition minted with new_composition and run an A/B. Use this to seed a composition (add media clips) or make targeted edits (set a crop intent, reorder clips, set the format). CAPTIONS FOR EDITED TIMELINES: after saving all clip edits, call again with {type:"captions.fromComposition", trackId} to build captions from every audible clip on that track, honoring trims, exclusions and placement. Clips must have duration matching playable source duration divided by playbackRate; unsupported timing fails explicitly. Re-run it after later timeline edits; captions do not update automatically. {type:"captions.fromTranscript", mediaId, window?} instead replaces all captions from one media transcript, rebased to zero; it does not follow a montage. Style with {type:"setCaptionStyle", style}; or set explicit words with {type:"setCaptions", segments, style?} (e.g. translations or your own VO timings). Brand is NOT set here — it lives on the project (create_project / update_project with brandKitId — or PATCH /projects/:id over REST). CARDS: a {kind:"card", html, tokens} clip projects each `tokens` KEY `x` to the CSS custom property `--cf-x`, so the html must read it as `var(--cf-x)` — write `tokens:{"plate":"#0af"}` + `background:var(--cf-plate)`. Do NOT put dashes in the key: `"--plate"` becomes `--cf---plate` and your `var(--plate)` then resolves to NOTHING, which CSS silently degrades to a transparent background and black text. Responses carry `warnings[]` when a card reads a var nothing defines. SCENE SHOTS: for a 3D product shot — a tilted page screenshot, a lit laptop/phone showing a real screenshot, two-colour type, a colour-field backdrop, focus/grain/vignette and a camera move — use {type:"scene.add", clipId, newTrack|trackId, startTime, duration, scene, assets} and revise it with {type:"scene.update", clipId, scene?, assets?, startTime?, duration?}. You author a scene SPEC, never wrapper TSX; the server registers the component for you. There is NO built-in scene primitive in list_catalog — READ cueframe://scene-shot first for the JSON schema, the canonical V2 world-objects recipe with nested groups, slabs, pages, phones, laptops, world/screen text, admitted surfaces, camera motion, lighting, and the current resource limits.

response.description: MCP response view. Default compact omits repeated source bodies. Full returns the complete backend receipt or requested sources. This does not change the saved composition.

body.description: POST /projects/:id/composition/apply body — a batch of CompositionOps.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

__schema2.description: One scoped composition operation. Discriminated by `type` — `clip.add` / `clip.remove` / `clip.update` patch clips across any family; the rest cover markers, reframe, effects, captions, format, tracks, and the server-authoritative ripple recomputes. Every variant is `.strict()`: an unknown field is refused, not ignored.

__schema3.description: Add a clip to the timeline. The clip self-routes to a track by FAMILY (`clip.kind`, else derived from `source.kind`, else the target track) — a `media` clip MUST carry `kind` (video|audio|image) or a `trackId`, else it is rejected as ambiguous. `trackId` targets an existing SAME-family track; `newTrack:true` (with optional pinned `newTrackId`) creates a fresh track of that family, appended at the BACK (the highest index, painted under every other track); raise it with `reorderTracks` (index 0 is the top layer).

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

kenBurns.description: Still-image motion. When unset, an image clip slowly pushes in (`in`) unless its fit is `contain` or it keyframes scale, position or rotation, so a keyframed clip renders exactly its keyframed values; set `none` for a still that holds.

audioRole.description: Mix role. A role sets the clip's default gain when it has no `volume` or `volumeDb`: vo 0 dB, sfx -6 dB, music -8 dB (-16 dB when any vo clip exists), ambience -22 dB. Set `volumeDb: 0` to keep a role and play the source at its own level.

html.description: Self-contained card markup sized to the format's pixel frame. Motion comes from frame-driven vars, never @keyframes or transition: --cf-frame, --cf-t (seconds), --cf-fps, --cf-duration, --cf-progress, --cf-ease, --cf-enter, --cf-exit. Visible copy goes in the html as plain text. Wrap a run in <span data-cf-split="words"> or "chars" and each unit becomes its own span carrying --cf-i (its index, the group carries --cf-n), so one rule staggers it (in chars, spaces count as units), e.g. opacity:clamp(0,calc(var(--cf-t)*4 - var(--cf-i)*.3),1). save_as_template binds that copy with textParams match.

tokens.description: Style values the html reads as CSS custom properties: key x becomes --cf-x, so never put dashes in a key. Use tokens for colours and sizes, not visible copy.

startSec.description: Segment START in seconds, clip-relative. Segments tile the clip's duration in order.

endSec.description: Segment END in seconds, clip-relative. The span (endSec − startSec) is this segment's duration — the window `ease` ramps over.

focus.description: WHO/WHAT the camera tracks this segment (the reframe center), selected by `mode`: `frame-center` = no tracking, hold the geometric center (static/graphic footage, or a pure zoom); `point` = lock to a fixed source-normalized {x,y} (a non-moving on-screen element); `face` = track a detected face by `faceId` (from get_media_context), with optional `shotScale` close|standard|wide for tightness; `all-faces` = frame the bounding box of every detected face (group/ensemble shots); `active-speaker` = follow whoever is speaking (diarized talking-head / podcast). Pick by what the beat is about; pair with `zoom` for how tight.

intent.description: Optional editorial LABEL for diff/log readability (e.g. 'speaker-tight', 'wide-context'). Cosmetic — NOT honored by the derive math and excluded from the variant cache key.

zoom.description: How TIGHT the framing is — the fraction of the source the output viewport shows. <1 punches IN (a smaller source fraction, magnified to fill the frame); 1 = the full frame (no crop). ~0.6–0.8 is a moderate push-in, ~0.5 a tight close-up, 0.1 the maximum zoom. There is NO zoom-OUT past the full frame (max 1). Omit for the full frame. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `focus.shotScale`: a face-tracked shot is sized EITHER by the editorial scale (shotScale, calibrated to the detected face) OR by an explicit zoom — never both.

ease.description: Zoom/center ramp DURATIONS in SECONDS at this segment's edges — NOT a unitless 0–1 curve. ~0.3–0.6s reads as a snappy push; >1s reads sluggish. Keep `in` + `out` ≤ the segment's duration (endSec − startSec): the two edges share the span, so to ramp across the WHOLE segment set one edge to the full duration and the other to 0. Omit for an instant cut to this framing.

bias.description: Optional FINE framing nudge off the focus center, source-normalized in [−0.3, 0.3]. A small correction (headroom, rule-of-thirds), NOT a reframe — use `focus`/`zoom` for the actual shot. Omit (treated as 0) to sit dead-center on the focus.

__schema13.description: Ease-IN ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment START.

__schema14.description: Ease-OUT ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment END.

__schema41.description: Remove a clip by id (located across every track).

__schema44.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `keyframes: null`) ONE keyframed channel of a clip: `opacity`, `scale`, `rotation`, `position.x`, `position.y` or `volume`, with at least two keyframes `{time, value, ease?}` in any order. `time` is seconds from the clip's own start (0 to its duration); `value` uses the property's own unit, as its scalar: opacity 0-1, scale a multiplier, rotation degrees, position.x/position.y a FRACTION of the frame (0.5 = centre, never px), volume 0-4. Each keyframe's optional `ease` shapes the segment ARRIVING at it, in HyperFrames' vocabulary: `none` (linear, the default), named eases such as `power2.out`, `back.out`, `expo.inOut`, `spring-gentle`, `hold`, or `custom(M0,0 Cx1,y1 x2,y2 1,1)` (a cubic, x in [0,1]). Before its first keyframe a channel holds its first value, after its last it holds the last; a channel OVERRIDES the clip's scalar (`opacity`, `scale`, `rotation`, `position`). The op REPLACES that property's keyframes; other channels are untouched. Volume keyframes are linear and only for a video or audio media clip. Trims and splits keep every keyframe on its content. Keyframes are stored as HyperFrames tweens (`tweens`) and automation (`automation`) on the clip; author them with this op, not `clip.update`.

__schema50.description: Patch an existing clip by id (cross-family). The patch is a partial TimelineClip. NOTE: `source` is REPLACED wholesale — the patch merges at the top level only, so a partial `source` WIPES the source fields you omit. Patch the whole source object when changing it. (To change reframe/excluded ranges, prefer setCropIntents / addExcludedRange, not a source patch.)

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

__schema64.description: Remove EVERY clip sourced from a given mediaId (e.g. after deleting that media).

__schema67.description: Replace the overlay channel wholesale with the given clips (bulk set, not a merge).

__schema70.description: Add a timeline marker (a named time point/range; carry extensions in `metadata`).

__schema76.description: Patch a marker's fields by id (partial merge).

__schema80.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `segments: null`) the camera/reframe channel on a MEDIA clip — the time-aligned source→output viewport (focus, zoom, ease, bias). This is the PREFERRED way to author reframing; do NOT reframe via a whole-source `clip.update` patch. Segments tile the clip's duration.

__schema84.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `effects: []`) a clip's EFFECT channel — the pinned component clip wrappers stacked onto that clip, each `{id, component, window}`: a unique `id`, the wrapper component's execution pin as `component`, and `window: {startTime, duration}` in seconds. The built-in primitive effects were removed: a stored one reads, and save and render refuse it (`effect_retired`), so clear it with `effects: []`. WHOLESALE: the array REPLACES the clip's current effects, so send the full stack (read the clip first to add one). This is the ONLY way to change effects on an existing clip — do NOT reach for a `clip.update` patch, whose top-level merge is the source-clobbering footgun documented above.

__schema88.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `inputTransform: null`) how a MEDIA's pixels are decoded into the working color space, for every clip of that media: `{version: 1, id, table?, ycbcr?}` with `id` one of rec709, insta360-ilog, custom-lut, apple-log. `custom-lut` is a camera LUT (log → Rec.709, e.g. DJI's D-Log M LUT): it requires `table: {mediaId, sha256, enabled}` naming an uploaded .cube LUT, and its output is read as Rec.709 footage; the others take no table. `ycbcr: {matrix, range}` overrides the source's signalled YCbCr matrix and range. The entry lives in the composition's `media` map; the media must be used by a clip in this composition, and removing its last clip removes the entry. To set a camera input for many media, send one `setMediaInputTransform` per media in a single `apply_composition` call.

__schema92.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `color: null`) a video media clip's color correction, WHOLESALE: `{version: 1, enabled, grade, looks, display?, creative?}`. `grade` holds every primary control: `exposure` in stops (-4..4) and `contrast`, `highlights`, `shadows`, `whites`, `blacks`, `temperature`, `tint`, `vibrance`, `saturation` each -1..1 (0 = neutral). `looks` (at most 2), `display` and `creative` name uploaded .cube LUTs as `{mediaId, sha256, enabled}`; `creative` adds `strength` 0..1. `display` may instead name a bundled film look as `{bundled, enabled}`, `bundled` one of daylight-negative, tungsten-negative, soft-negative, slide, black-and-white. `halation?: {enabled, amount 0..0.5, radius (picture heights) 0.0005..0.02, threshold 0..16, tint [r,g,b] 0..1}`; `grain?: {enabled, profile (a film look id), gauge super8|super16|super35|65mm, amount 0..2, size 0.5..4, seed uint32}`. Film presets are whole values, applied by replacing `display`, `halation` and `grain` with exactly what the preset names (absent = removed), writing only the grade keys it names, `display` as `{bundled, enabled: true}`, `halation`/`grain` with `enabled: true`, and grain `seed` kept or any uint32. Presets: {"id":"daylight-negative","name":"Daylight Negative","display":"daylight-negative","halation":{"amount":0.015,"radius":0.0026795284030010718,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.33333333333333337,0]},"grain":{"profile":"daylight-negative","gauge":"super35","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"tungsten-negative","name":"Tungsten Negative","display":"tungsten-negative","halation":{"amount":0.015,"radius":0.0026795284030010718,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.33333333333333337,0]},"grain":{"profile":"tungsten-negative","gauge":"super35","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"soft-negative","name":"Soft Negative","display":"soft-negative","halation":{"amount":0.015,"radius":0.0034833869239013935,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.33333333333333337,0]},"grain":{"profile":"soft-negative","gauge":"super35","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"slide","name":"Slide","display":"slide","halation":{"amount":0.015,"radius":0.0034833869239013935,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.33333333333333337,0]},"grain":{"profile":"slide","gauge":"super35","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"black-and-white","name":"Black and White","display":"black-and-white","halation":{"amount":0.015,"radius":0.0026795284030010718,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.33333333333333337,0]},"grain":{"profile":"black-and-white","gauge":"super35","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"grain-only-fine","name":"Fine grain","grain":{"profile":"daylight-negative","gauge":"65mm","amount":1,"size":1}}; {"id":"halation-only","name":"Halation","halation":{"amount":0.08,"radius":0.0026795284030010718,"threshold":0,"tint":[1,0.25,0]}}. `enabled: false` bypasses the whole correction. Only a media clip on a video track takes color.

__schema96.description: Merge style overrides (font/color/position/emphasis) onto the composition's caption layer. Partial — omitted fields keep their current value; creates the caption container if absent.

fontSize.description: Font size as % of composition height (1-15, default 5). NOT px.

region.description: Optional caption layout box {x,y,w,h} in normalized output-frame coordinates. Overrides position; text starts at its top edge and wraps/pages within its width and height.

letterSpacing.description: Base caption glyph spacing in pixels.

wordGapEm.description: Gap between caption runs as a multiple of base font size; default 0.35.

lineGapEm.description: Gap between caption lines as a multiple of base font size; default 0.25.

emphasisPlateReveal.description: Grow a shared emphasis plate as saved words appear while reserving its final layout width.

annotationStrokeWidth.description: Annotation stroke width in its 100×100 SVG coordinate system; default 4.

annotationTexture.description: Native annotation stroke finish; default clean.

__schema104.description: Set the caption compositing plane. Use `behind-subject` to place captions behind the segmented foreground subject; use `front` for conventional captions above all video layers.

__schema107.description: Replace the caption SEGMENTS wholesale — author the word-timed caption layer directly (each segment = one sentence/page of `words` with timeline-ms `startMs`/`endMs`, optional `emphasis`). This is how a client with its OWN word timings (e.g. a generated VO take) gets word-synced captions without a source transcript; the compose lane's transcript slice writes the same layer. `style`, when given, merges with setCaptionStyle semantics; an omitted style keeps the existing one. Renderer paginates within a segment and never pools words across two — keep segments sentence-bounded.

startMs.description: Word start on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

endMs.description: Word end on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

__schema111.description: Replace native caption placements without changing transcript words or timings. Each layout references a half-open word-index range in one saved segment; a one-word range is valid. region places that group independently, optional bounded scale/rotation/style changes its look, and holdThroughWordIndex keeps it visible through a later saved word in the same segment. All words in a placed range occupy one page; rendering refuses a range that cannot fit its box, so enlarge region or split the range. The box reserves horizontal space of 1.6 font sizes and vertical space of 0.8 font sizes for padding, with at most three lines. Unreferenced words keep the default caption layout. Word ranges must not overlap. Reapply after caption regeneration or timeline cuts.

wordEndIndex.description: Exclusive word index in the saved caption segment.

fontSize.description: Font size as % of composition height (1-15, default 5). NOT px.

letterSpacing.description: Base caption glyph spacing in pixels.

wordGapEm.description: Gap between caption runs as a multiple of base font size; default 0.35.

lineGapEm.description: Gap between caption lines as a multiple of base font size; default 0.25.

emphasisPlateReveal.description: Grow a shared emphasis plate as saved words appear while reserving its final layout width.

annotationStrokeWidth.description: Annotation stroke width in its 100×100 SVG coordinate system; default 4.

annotationTexture.description: Native annotation stroke finish; default clean.

holdThroughWordIndex.description: Inclusive saved-word index in this segment. The layout stays visible until that word ends.

__schema114.description: Author a scene shot and place it on a dedicated overlay track. The host validates the scene, generates and registers an immutable wrapper component source, and emits the ordinary track/clip operations carrying `props.componentRef` — you edit a scene SPEC, never wrapper TSX or a source hash. Registration and the composition update are ONE undoable edit; a failure publishes nothing and leaves no clip pointing at an unresolved source. REQUIRED: `clipId`, `startTime`, `duration`, `scene` and `assets` (send `{}` when no layer references a slot), plus EXACTLY ONE of `trackId` (an existing dedicated scene track) or `newTrack: true` (mint one). A minted scene track is appended at the BACK like every new track, so it paints under existing tracks; raise it with `reorderTracks` (index 0 is the top layer). That track holds scene-shot clips and gaps only — no generic component/primitive/media clips in v1 — and existing generic overlay tracks are unaffected. Scene clips use front zPlane and full-frame placement: outer per-clip `region`, `position`, `scale`, `rotation`, `fit`, `effects`, keyframes (`tweens`/`automation`), `params.transition`, `params.sequenceGroup` and internal fadeIn/fadeOut are REFUSED with a path, because the shot's own layer transforms are the single transform owner. TEXT: `space: "screen"` text is composed above the world result, stays fixed in the frame and stays sharp through focus; `space: "world"` text is rasterized into the 3D scene, moves with the camera and is occluded by geometry. Screenshots and world text are UNLIT and colour-managed so product UI colours are not tinted by the studio lighting, while device bodies are lit and cast shadows; an unlit surface still occludes. SCOPE GAP (pre-existing, neither closed nor changed by scene shots): global wrap effects — composition-level grades and camera effects — do not reach front-overlay clips, so they do not affect a scene shot. Author the look INSIDE the shot (`post.grain`, `post.vignette`, `post.focus`, `backdrop`, `environment`) instead. DISCOVERY: there is no built-in scene primitive to look up in list_catalog; the wrapper this operation registers appears afterwards as an ordinary INSTALLED component under the existing catalog rules. ASSETS: `assets` binds each slot name a layer references to a media id in the same project, and the slot's declared KIND decides what it admits — an image slot takes PNG, JPEG or WebP, a video slot MP4 or WebM. Binding the wrong kind is refused with the slot's path.

__schema123.description: A version-2 scene shot: a self-contained 3D world-object shot that scene.add / scene.update materializes into an ordinary component clip. The shot owns its layers, camera, lighting, backdrop and normalized local animation; the composition owns start, duration, ordering, cuts and transitions. Coordinates are REFERENCE PIXELS: origin at frame centre, +X right, +Y down, +Z toward the viewer. referenceSize must have the SAME aspect ratio as the composition format; mismatch fails instead of cropping. At equal aspect ratio the shot scales uniformly by outputWidth/referenceWidth. A segment's easing belongs to the keyframe it ARRIVES at; the first keyframe has no easing. Authoring limits: 32 layers, 4 devices, 16 distinct image slots, 256 keyframes per channel, 2048 keyframes per shot. Version 2 supports nested groups, procedural slab/page/phone/laptop objects, screen- and world-space text, admitted image/component/video surfaces, fixed photographic and generated studio environments, transparent/solid/linear/radial backdrops, constraints, focus, grain and vignette. Raw HTML, custom shader props, imported GLB models, arbitrary external HDR environments, skeletal animation and physics are refused with an exact field path.

assetSlot.description: Image asset slot name bound by the clip assets map; never a URL.

bakeScale.description: Optional authored scale. Preparation defaults omission to 2 and may auto-raise it to 3.

__schema194.description: Revise a scene shot in place by clip id. Send a replacement `scene` and/or `assets`; timing changes use the ordinary clip timing fields (`startTime`, `duration`, `transitionIn`). Omitted fields keep their persisted values and the MERGED result is re-validated as a whole, so a partial edit cannot leave the shot invalid. Changing only values or asset IDs updates props and bindings and REUSES the pinned source; changing the referenced SLOT SET regenerates the wrapper manifest and registers a new immutable source version atomically. Undo restores the source reference, spec, bindings and timing together. Topology, asset bindings, text content, font properties, device kind and colours are STATIC within a shot's animation — change them here (a revised spec) rather than trying to animate them. This is not a source trim or slip: a shortened or extended clip resamples the SAME normalized animation over its new duration, and trim/slip requests on generated animation are rejected rather than reinterpreted as media trims. In one batch, `scene.update` may target a shot added by an earlier `scene.add`. ASSETS: `assets` binds each slot name a layer references to a media id in the same project, and the slot's declared KIND decides what it admits — an image slot takes PNG, JPEG or WebP, a video slot MP4 or WebM. Binding the wrong kind is refused with the slot's path.

__schema202.description: Materialize a clip's SOURCE-media temporal GRID as timeline markers — the rhythm authority you cut to. `grid:"beat"` reads a MUSIC bed's beat map (get_media_context.beatGrid), `grid:"word"` the VO word onsets (wordGrid); each grid point is projected from media time to TIMELINE time through the clip's placement (startTime, trim, playbackRate, excludedRanges) and written as a `kind:"beat"|"word"` marker (`metadata.sourceClipId` set). Points outside the clip's visible window are skipped. Re-running REPLACES the prior markers from the same clip+grid (idempotent). Land cuts and transition MIDPOINTS on the markers (a 0.5s transition starts 0.25s before its marker). `maxMarkers` (default 500, ceiling 2000) — exceeding it fails loud with the count. `grid:"shot"` is not yet exposed (shot_grid_unavailable). The target must be a media clip; absent evidence fails loud (grid_unavailable) naming how to get it (declare audioRole:"music" at ingest / transcribe).

__schema207.description: Attach caption CONTENT from the media's cached transcript — no pasting words. ROUTE-MATERIALIZED like materializeGrid: the server slices the word-timed transcript to `window` (source seconds; absent = the whole media), rebases times, sentence-splits into segments, and applies it as `setCaptions`. 422 media_no_transcript when the media has no transcript or no words in the window. For your OWN word timings use setCaptions directly. For edited multi-clip timelines, use captions.fromComposition after saving the edits; that operation projects all selected track clips, trims, exclusions, and placements.

__schema211.description: Snapshot word-timed captions from the SAVED edits on one explicit enabled video or audio track. The host reads each source media transcript, projects words through clip trim, excluded ranges and placement, then replaces the caption segments. This is route-materialized to setCaptions; call it AFTER persisting clip edits and call it again when those edits change. The existing caption style and depth are preserved. Missing transcripts, unsupported clips, inconsistent clip durations, and overlapping audible clips fail loud. Playback rate scales source word times and playable duration on both audio and video tracks.

__schema214.description: Set the output format — `aspectRatio` (16:9|9:16|1:1|4:5) plus optional `fps` and `resolution`. Merges: an omitted field keeps the current value.

__schema217.description: Add an EMPTY track of a given family (video|audio|image|overlay|effect). Optional pinned `id`. The new track is appended, so it starts at the BACK: index 0 is the top layer and higher indices are further back (see `reorderTracks`). Track order is the paint order for every family: a card on a track behind a video or image track draws behind it.

__schema222.description: Remove a track AND all its clips by id.

__schema225.description: Patch a track's `name` / `enabled` by id. Track volume is retired: set each clip's own volume.

__schema229.description: Move a track from one index to another. ORDER: index 0 is the TOP layer, not the bottom — moving a backdrop to index 0 puts it in FRONT of everything and hides the composition. Higher index = further back. Track order is the paint order for every family, so cards, overlays, images and video interleave by index: a backdrop card, a screenshot and a foreground card on three tracks stack in that order. The one exception is `zPlane:"behind-subject"`, which moves the overlay inside its host clip, behind the segmented foreground.

__schema233.description: Move a clip to another SAME-family track, optionally at a new `newStartTime`.

__schema238.description: Duplicate a clip by id. Pin `newClipId` to make the copy's id deterministic (required for a clean undo/inverse).

__schema242.description: Server-authoritative: delete the [start,end] time window (seconds) and ripple every downstream clip/marker/caption earlier to close the gap. Cuts apply sequentially in TIMELINE seconds: each cut moves everything after it, so a later cut's coordinates go stale once an earlier one lands. Plan several cuts back to front (latest first), or send them as one `cutRanges`. To drop spans inside one clip, `addExcludedRange` takes SOURCE seconds and is order-independent.

Every range is in timeline seconds of the composition as it is BEFORE this op, in any order; overlapping and touching ranges merge. Each must satisfy 0 <= start < end <= the timeline's end. The cuts apply back to front with exactly `cutAndRipple`'s ripple (every track, markers and derived captions move earlier), so no coordinate goes stale.

__schema250.description: Server-authoritative: shift everything at/after `time` (seconds) by `amount` seconds (+ opens a gap, − closes one).

__schema254.description: Server-authoritative: exclude a [sourceStart,sourceEnd] span (seconds) of a clip's SOURCE (an internal trim) and ripple downstream — the preferred way to drop a sub-range vs a source patch. html.description: Self-contained card markup sized to the format's pixel frame. Motion comes from frame-driven vars, never @keyframes or transition: --cf-frame, --cf-t (seconds), --cf-fps, --cf-duration, --cf-progress, --cf-ease, --cf-enter, --cf-exit. Visible copy goes in the html as plain text. Wrap a run in <span data-cf-split="words"> or "chars" and each unit becomes its own span carrying --cf-i (its index, the group carries --cf-n), so one rule staggers it (in chars, spaces count as units), e.g. opacity:clamp(0,calc(var(--cf-t)*4 - var(--cf-i)*.3),1). save_as_template binds that copy with textParams match.

tokens.description: Style values the html reads as CSS custom properties: key x becomes --cf-x, so never put dashes in a key. Use tokens for colours and sizes, not visible copy.

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

startSec.description: Segment START in seconds, clip-relative. Segments tile the clip's duration in order.

endSec.description: Segment END in seconds, clip-relative. The span (endSec − startSec) is this segment's duration — the window `ease` ramps over.

focus.description: WHO/WHAT the camera tracks this segment (the reframe center), selected by `mode`: `frame-center` = no tracking, hold the geometric center (static/graphic footage, or a pure zoom); `point` = lock to a fixed source-normalized {x,y} (a non-moving on-screen element); `face` = track a detected face by `faceId` (from get_media_context), with optional `shotScale` close|standard|wide for tightness; `all-faces` = frame the bounding box of every detected face (group/ensemble shots); `active-speaker` = follow whoever is speaking (diarized talking-head / podcast). Pick by what the beat is about; pair with `zoom` for how tight.

intent.description: Optional editorial LABEL for diff/log readability (e.g. 'speaker-tight', 'wide-context'). Cosmetic — NOT honored by the derive math and excluded from the variant cache key.

zoom.description: How TIGHT the framing is — the fraction of the source the output viewport shows. <1 punches IN (a smaller source fraction, magnified to fill the frame); 1 = the full frame (no crop). ~0.6–0.8 is a moderate push-in, ~0.5 a tight close-up, 0.1 the maximum zoom. There is NO zoom-OUT past the full frame (max 1). Omit for the full frame. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `focus.shotScale`: a face-tracked shot is sized EITHER by the editorial scale (shotScale, calibrated to the detected face) OR by an explicit zoom — never both.

ease.description: Zoom/center ramp DURATIONS in SECONDS at this segment's edges — NOT a unitless 0–1 curve. ~0.3–0.6s reads as a snappy push; >1s reads sluggish. Keep `in` + `out` ≤ the segment's duration (endSec − startSec): the two edges share the span, so to ramp across the WHOLE segment set one edge to the full duration and the other to 0. Omit for an instant cut to this framing.

bias.description: Optional FINE framing nudge off the focus center, source-normalized in [−0.3, 0.3]. A small correction (headroom, rule-of-thirds), NOT a reframe — use `focus`/`zoom` for the actual shot. Omit (treated as 0) to sit dead-center on the focus.

tools.description:
Create and store a custom component for the tenant: a native scene that arranges its declared images and videos as tiles in 3D space. Returns the ComponentResponse (id + metadata) you can then reference from a composition. No project arg — components are tenant-scoped. SOURCE CONTRACT (version 4; the server instructions' Component Contract has the full rules and an example): send the complete source object {version:4, componentId, template, manifest, definition}. `template` is one sub-composition: a root
holding
, and one inline script ending in __cfScene.mount({ root: document.getElementById('root'), component, variables: __hyperframes.getVariables() }). data-composition-variables is the definition's projection (scalar inputSchema properties, then manifest slots). The manifest is {version:4, runtime:'hyperframes', hfContract:1, kind:'scene', assets, graphics:{api:'webgl2',…}, alphaPolicy}; slots are image or video. A version-3 source is retired and refused as component_source_retired. Place it with execution {version:4, componentId, sourceVersionId, params, seed, assets:{ slot: mediaId }} and placement {version:3, kind:'clip'}; slots never travel in params.

error.description: Human-readable failure message. Pair with `errorCode` for a stable, machine-readable code an agent runner can branch on.

errorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable error code (e.g. `render_pipeline_unavailable`, `render_route_missing`, `render_pipeline_failed`). Null when status is not `error` or unavailable for an older render.

errorDetails.description: Structured failure context — `{ targetUrl?, upstreamStatus?, upstreamCode?, attemptedAt? }`. Surfaced so agent runners can distinguish operator-config issues from upstream-down vs route-missing without parsing `error`.

category.description: Failure taxonomy when status is `error`; null otherwise. `authoring` = deterministic defect in YOUR composition/request — fix it, retrying is futile; `transient` = temporary pipeline/infra failure — safe to retry_render; `internal` = unexpected server fault — retry once then escalate. Mirrors the render.failed webhook's `category`.

retryable.description: Whether re-attempting the SAME render can succeed (status `error`); null otherwise. true → call retry_render. false → deterministic (category authoring/internal); fix the composition first — retry_render alone reproduces it. Mirrors the render.failed webhook's `retryable`.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the render's most recent progress update. Compute staleness = now − updatedAt to distinguish a wedged render from a slow one and decide whether to wait, cancel, or retry.

compositionId.description: The composition this render froze at create time (the project's active one, or the compositionId the request named). Null on renders minted before this was recorded.

format.description: The resolved output format the render was encoded at (aspectRatio, fps, resolution): the frozen composition's, after any create-time scale override. Null on legacy rows.

engine.description: The render engine the row was minted for. Null on rows minted before the engine was recorded.

completedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the render reached its terminal status (complete, error or cancelled); null while it runs. Pair with createdAt for the wall time.

outputDurationSec.description: The output's length in seconds (the composition timeline's, or the preview window's), as billed. Null on legacy rows.

preview.description: The scoped preview window when this is a preview_clip render; null for a full deliverable.

listUsd.description: A2 money stamp: the metered event's LIST price (USD), stamped at the success terminal (exports for deliverable renders, compose_capture for A8 previews). A plan allowance may zero the actual invoice line — this is the list price, never a Stripe charge. Absent while running, on failure, and for x402 orgs (on-chain receipts). Mirrors the get_usage ledger.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories surfaced at render-CREATE (omitted when none, and on GET — create-time only).

tools.name: create_upload
tools.title: Create Upload
tools.description: Ingest a LOCAL file — bytes you hold, when there is no public URL to hand import_media (prefer import_media whenever the bytes already sit at an https URL). TWO steps: (1) this tool reserves a media item and returns { id, uploadUrl, expiresAt } — a short-lived PUT URL. PUT the raw file bytes to uploadUrl over HTTPS with your declared Content-Type (≤ ~5 GB per PUT). (2) call finalize_upload({ mediaItemId: id }) to start processing. Body: filename, contentType (allowed enum), size (bytes). Thereafter it is async exactly like import_media: poll list_media for processingStatus, or register a webhook (create_webhook on media.completed). Use the returned id with get_media_context, suggest_briefs, or as a composition source.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.title: Create Webhook
tools.description: Register a webhook so long-running jobs notify you instead of blocking on wait_job — the right pattern for fan-out/async agents. Pass url + events — ONE terminal event per job kind with status INSIDE the payload (render.completed, compose.completed, media.completed, suggest.completed) plus checkpoint.ready (a held compose paused for review). DELIVERY: a POST { event, timestamp, projectId?, data } with Standard-Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature: v1,<base64>); the secret (whsec_<base64>) is returned ONCE — verify the RAW body with new Webhook(secret).verify(rawBody, headers). ACTIVATION is synchronous: CueFrame POSTs a signed webhook.verify challenge and your endpoint must reply 2xx echoing data.token — otherwise it returns status:"pending" and receives NO events (recover with verify_webhook, no delete/recreate). Read the cueframe://webhook-events resource (or GET /webhooks/events) for the full contract + every event's data shape BEFORE building your receiver.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

status.description: active = ownership verified + receiving events; pending = challenge not echoed, inactive.

secret.description: Standard Webhooks signing secret, format `whsec_<base64>`. Returned ONCE at create; rotate = delete + recreate. Every delivery carries `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` (unix seconds), and `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>` (HMAC-SHA256 over `{id}.{timestamp}.{rawBody}`). Verify with any Standard-Webhooks library (`standardwebhooks` / `svix`): `new Webhook(secret).verify(rawBody, headers)`.

verification.description: Present ONLY when ownership verification did not complete (status:"pending"). CueFrame POSTs a signed `webhook.verify` challenge whose `data.token` your endpoint must echo in a 2xx to activate; `reason` is one of token_not_echoed | non_2xx_<code> | unreachable | ssrf_blocked. A pending webhook receives no events — fix the receiver and POST /webhooks/:id/verify (no delete/recreate needed). See GET /webhooks/events for the full contract.

tools.name: derive_composition
tools.title: Derive Composition
tools.description: Derive a reframed SIBLING composition for a different aspect ratio (the agent-native Auto-Reframe / Magic-Resize). Pass projectId + body { fromCompositionId, targetFormat: { aspectRatio, fps?, resolution? } }. CueFrame copies the source composition's authored intent and content-aware-reframes every clip for the new aspect (point/face/active-speaker focus), then saves a new independent composition in the same project. Returns { compositionId } — render it with create_render, or refine it with apply_composition. Use this to make 9:16 + 1:1 + 4:5 cuts from one 16:9 edit. (To only change resolution within the SAME aspect, pass create_render.format instead — that is a scale-only export override, not a new composition.)

This is how you copy media OUT of a library: fetch the URL directly (no auth header) and PUT the bytes elsewhere with create_upload, or hand it to import_media on another account. Works as soon as the upload or import is stored, before processing completes. The URL expires at `expiresAt` (about an hour) — call again for a fresh one rather than caching it. expiresAt.description: Expiry of this URL in UTC (about one hour).

tools.name: editorial_apply
tools.title: Editorial Apply
tools.description: Commit an integrated editorial edit to the saved project composition with both runExpectedRevision and guarded composition fields. Preserve the observed concurrency basis and the composition journal identity: nested composition.commandId must equal composition.clientId + ":" + composition.sequence. The session call commandId is a separate HTTP request identity.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

operation.description: One scoped composition operation. Discriminated by `type` — `clip.add` / `clip.remove` / `clip.update` patch clips across any family; the rest cover markers, reframe, effects, captions, format, tracks, and the server-authoritative ripple recomputes. Every variant is `.strict()`: an unknown field is refused, not ignored.

__schema7.description: Add a clip to the timeline. The clip self-routes to a track by FAMILY (`clip.kind`, else derived from `source.kind`, else the target track) — a `media` clip MUST carry `kind` (video|audio|image) or a `trackId`, else it is rejected as ambiguous. `trackId` targets an existing SAME-family track; `newTrack:true` (with optional pinned `newTrackId`) creates a fresh track of that family, appended at the BACK (the highest index, painted under every other track); raise it with `reorderTracks` (index 0 is the top layer).

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

kenBurns.description: Still-image motion. When unset, an image clip slowly pushes in (`in`) unless its fit is `contain` or it keyframes scale, position or rotation, so a keyframed clip renders exactly its keyframed values; set `none` for a still that holds.

audioRole.description: Mix role. A role sets the clip's default gain when it has no `volume` or `volumeDb`: vo 0 dB, sfx -6 dB, music -8 dB (-16 dB when any vo clip exists), ambience -22 dB. Set `volumeDb: 0` to keep a role and play the source at its own level.

html.description: Self-contained card markup sized to the format's pixel frame. Motion comes from frame-driven vars, never @keyframes or transition: --cf-frame, --cf-t (seconds), --cf-fps, --cf-duration, --cf-progress, --cf-ease, --cf-enter, --cf-exit. Visible copy goes in the html as plain text. Wrap a run in <span data-cf-split="words"> or "chars" and each unit becomes its own span carrying --cf-i (its index, the group carries --cf-n), so one rule staggers it (in chars, spaces count as units), e.g. opacity:clamp(0,calc(var(--cf-t)*4 - var(--cf-i)*.3),1). save_as_template binds that copy with textParams match.

tokens.description: Style values the html reads as CSS custom properties: key x becomes --cf-x, so never put dashes in a key. Use tokens for colours and sizes, not visible copy.

startSec.description: Segment START in seconds, clip-relative. Segments tile the clip's duration in order.

endSec.description: Segment END in seconds, clip-relative. The span (endSec − startSec) is this segment's duration — the window `ease` ramps over.

focus.description: WHO/WHAT the camera tracks this segment (the reframe center), selected by `mode`: `frame-center` = no tracking, hold the geometric center (static/graphic footage, or a pure zoom); `point` = lock to a fixed source-normalized {x,y} (a non-moving on-screen element); `face` = track a detected face by `faceId` (from get_media_context), with optional `shotScale` close|standard|wide for tightness; `all-faces` = frame the bounding box of every detected face (group/ensemble shots); `active-speaker` = follow whoever is speaking (diarized talking-head / podcast). Pick by what the beat is about; pair with `zoom` for how tight.

intent.description: Optional editorial LABEL for diff/log readability (e.g. 'speaker-tight', 'wide-context'). Cosmetic — NOT honored by the derive math and excluded from the variant cache key.

zoom.description: How TIGHT the framing is — the fraction of the source the output viewport shows. <1 punches IN (a smaller source fraction, magnified to fill the frame); 1 = the full frame (no crop). ~0.6–0.8 is a moderate push-in, ~0.5 a tight close-up, 0.1 the maximum zoom. There is NO zoom-OUT past the full frame (max 1). Omit for the full frame. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `focus.shotScale`: a face-tracked shot is sized EITHER by the editorial scale (shotScale, calibrated to the detected face) OR by an explicit zoom — never both.

ease.description: Zoom/center ramp DURATIONS in SECONDS at this segment's edges — NOT a unitless 0–1 curve. ~0.3–0.6s reads as a snappy push; >1s reads sluggish. Keep `in` + `out` ≤ the segment's duration (endSec − startSec): the two edges share the span, so to ramp across the WHOLE segment set one edge to the full duration and the other to 0. Omit for an instant cut to this framing.

bias.description: Optional FINE framing nudge off the focus center, source-normalized in [−0.3, 0.3]. A small correction (headroom, rule-of-thirds), NOT a reframe — use `focus`/`zoom` for the actual shot. Omit (treated as 0) to sit dead-center on the focus.

__schema17.description: Ease-IN ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment START.

__schema18.description: Ease-OUT ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment END.

__schema45.description: Remove a clip by id (located across every track).

__schema48.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `keyframes: null`) ONE keyframed channel of a clip: `opacity`, `scale`, `rotation`, `position.x`, `position.y` or `volume`, with at least two keyframes `{time, value, ease?}` in any order. `time` is seconds from the clip's own start (0 to its duration); `value` uses the property's own unit, as its scalar: opacity 0-1, scale a multiplier, rotation degrees, position.x/position.y a FRACTION of the frame (0.5 = centre, never px), volume 0-4. Each keyframe's optional `ease` shapes the segment ARRIVING at it, in HyperFrames' vocabulary: `none` (linear, the default), named eases such as `power2.out`, `back.out`, `expo.inOut`, `spring-gentle`, `hold`, or `custom(M0,0 Cx1,y1 x2,y2 1,1)` (a cubic, x in [0,1]). Before its first keyframe a channel holds its first value, after its last it holds the last; a channel OVERRIDES the clip's scalar (`opacity`, `scale`, `rotation`, `position`). The op REPLACES that property's keyframes; other channels are untouched. Volume keyframes are linear and only for a video or audio media clip. Trims and splits keep every keyframe on its content. Keyframes are stored as HyperFrames tweens (`tweens`) and automation (`automation`) on the clip; author them with this op, not `clip.update`.

NOTE: `source` is REPLACED wholesale — the patch merges at the top level only, so a partial `source` WIPES the source fields you omit. Patch the whole source object when changing it. (To change reframe/excluded ranges, prefer setCropIntents / addExcludedRange, not a source patch.)

Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. __schema68.description: Remove EVERY clip sourced from a given mediaId (e.g. after deleting that media).

__schema71.description: Replace the overlay channel wholesale with the given clips (bulk set, not a merge).

__schema74.description: Add a timeline marker (a named time point/range; carry extensions in `metadata`).

__schema80.description: Patch a marker's fields by id (partial merge).

__schema84.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `segments: null`) the camera/reframe channel on a MEDIA clip — the time-aligned source→output viewport (focus, zoom, ease, bias). This is the PREFERRED way to author reframing; do NOT reframe via a whole-source `clip.update` patch. Segments tile the clip's duration.

__schema88.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `effects: []`) a clip's EFFECT channel — the pinned component clip wrappers stacked onto that clip, each `{id, component, window}`: a unique `id`, the wrapper component's execution pin as `component`, and `window: {startTime, duration}` in seconds. The built-in primitive effects were removed: a stored one reads, and save and render refuse it (`effect_retired`), so clear it with `effects: []`. WHOLESALE: the array REPLACES the clip's current effects, so send the full stack (read the clip first to add one). This is the ONLY way to change effects on an existing clip — do NOT reach for a `clip.update` patch, whose top-level merge is the source-clobbering footgun documented above.

__schema92.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `inputTransform: null`) how a MEDIA's pixels are decoded into the working color space, for every clip of that media: `{version: 1, id, table?, ycbcr?}` with `id` one of rec709, insta360-ilog, custom-lut, apple-log. `custom-lut` is a camera LUT (log → Rec.709, e.g. DJI's D-Log M LUT): it requires `table: {mediaId, sha256, enabled}` naming an uploaded .cube LUT, and its output is read as Rec.709 footage; the others take no table. `ycbcr: {matrix, range}` overrides the source's signalled YCbCr matrix and range. The entry lives in the composition's `media` map; the media must be used by a clip in this composition, and removing its last clip removes the entry. To set a camera input for many media, send one `setMediaInputTransform` per media in a single `apply_composition` call.

__schema96.description: Set (or CLEAR, with `color: null`) a video media clip's color correction, WHOLESALE: `{version: 1, enabled, grade, looks, display?, creative?}`. `grade` holds every primary control: `exposure` in stops (-4..4) and `contrast`, `highlights`, `shadows`, `whites`, `blacks`, `temperature`, `tint`, `vibrance`, `saturation` each -1..1 (0 = neutral). `looks` (at most 2), `display` and `creative` name uploaded .cube LUTs as `{mediaId, sha256, enabled}`; `creative` adds `strength` 0..1. `display` may instead name a bundled film look as `{bundled, enabled}`, `bundled` one of daylight-negative, tungsten-negative, soft-negative, slide, black-and-white. `halation?: {enabled, amount 0..0.5, radius (picture heights) 0.0005..0.02, threshold 0..16, tint [r,g,b] 0..1}`; `grain?: {enabled, profile (a film look id), gauge super8|super16|super35|65mm, amount 0..2, size 0.5..4, seed uint32}`. Only a media clip on a video track takes color.

__schema100.description: Merge style overrides (font/color/position/emphasis) onto the composition's caption layer. Partial — omitted fields keep their current value; creates the caption container if absent.

fontSize.description: Font size as % of composition height (1-15, default 5). NOT px.

region.description: Optional caption layout box {x,y,w,h} in normalized output-frame coordinates. Overrides position; text starts at its top edge and wraps/pages within its width and height.

letterSpacing.description: Base caption glyph spacing in pixels.

wordGapEm.description: Gap between caption runs as a multiple of base font size; default 0.35.

lineGapEm.description: Gap between caption lines as a multiple of base font size; default 0.25.

emphasisPlateReveal.description: Grow a shared emphasis plate as saved words appear while reserving its final layout width.

annotationStrokeWidth.description: Annotation stroke width in its 100×100 SVG coordinate system; default 4.

annotationTexture.description: Native annotation stroke finish; default clean.

__schema108.description: Set the caption compositing plane. Use `behind-subject` to place captions behind the segmented foreground subject; use `front` for conventional captions above all video layers.

__schema111.description: Replace the caption SEGMENTS wholesale — author the word-timed caption layer directly (each segment = one sentence/page of `words` with timeline-ms `startMs`/`endMs`, optional `emphasis`). This is how a client with its OWN word timings (e.g. a generated VO take) gets word-synced captions without a source transcript; the compose lane's transcript slice writes the same layer. `style`, when given, merges with setCaptionStyle semantics; an omitted style keeps the existing one. Renderer paginates within a segment and never pools words across two — keep segments sentence-bounded.

startMs.description: Word start on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

endMs.description: Word end on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

__schema115.description: Replace native caption placements without changing transcript words or timings. Each layout references a half-open word-index range in one saved segment; a one-word range is valid. region places that group independently, optional bounded scale/rotation/style changes its look, and holdThroughWordIndex keeps it visible through a later saved word in the same segment. All words in a placed range occupy one page; rendering refuses a range that cannot fit its box, so enlarge region or split the range. The box reserves horizontal space of 1.6 font sizes and vertical space of 0.8 font sizes for padding, with at most three lines. Unreferenced words keep the default caption layout. Word ranges must not overlap. Reapply after caption regeneration or timeline cuts.

wordEndIndex.description: Exclusive word index in the saved caption segment.

fontSize.description: Font size as % of composition height (1-15, default 5). NOT px.

letterSpacing.description: Base caption glyph spacing in pixels.

wordGapEm.description: Gap between caption runs as a multiple of base font size; default 0.35.

lineGapEm.description: Gap between caption lines as a multiple of base font size; default 0.25.

emphasisPlateReveal.description: Grow a shared emphasis plate as saved words appear while reserving its final layout width.

annotationStrokeWidth.description: Annotation stroke width in its 100×100 SVG coordinate system; default 4.

annotationTexture.description: Native annotation stroke finish; default clean.

holdThroughWordIndex.description: Inclusive saved-word index in this segment. The layout stays visible until that word ends.

__schema118.description: Author a scene shot and place it on a dedicated overlay track. The host validates the scene, generates and registers an immutable wrapper component source, and emits the ordinary track/clip operations carrying `props.componentRef` — you edit a scene SPEC, never wrapper TSX or a source hash. Registration and the composition update are ONE undoable edit; a failure publishes nothing and leaves no clip pointing at an unresolved source. REQUIRED: `clipId`, `startTime`, `duration`, `scene` and `assets` (send `{}` when no layer references a slot), plus EXACTLY ONE of `trackId` (an existing dedicated scene track) or `newTrack: true` (mint one). A minted scene track is appended at the BACK like every new track, so it paints under existing tracks; raise it with `reorderTracks` (index 0 is the top layer). That track holds scene-shot clips and gaps only — no generic component/primitive/media clips in v1 — and existing generic overlay tracks are unaffected. Scene clips use front zPlane and full-frame placement: outer per-clip `region`, `position`, `scale`, `rotation`, `fit`, `effects`, keyframes (`tweens`/`automation`), `params.transition`, `params.sequenceGroup` and internal fadeIn/fadeOut are REFUSED with a path, because the shot's own layer transforms are the single transform owner. TEXT: `space: "screen"` text is composed above the world result, stays fixed in the frame and stays sharp through focus; `space: "world"` text is rasterized into the 3D scene, moves with the camera and is occluded by geometry. Screenshots and world text are UNLIT and colour-managed so product UI colours are not tinted by the studio lighting, while device bodies are lit and cast shadows; an unlit surface still occludes. SCOPE GAP (pre-existing, neither closed nor changed by scene shots): global wrap effects — composition-level grades and camera effects — do not reach front-overlay clips, so they do not affect a scene shot. Author the look INSIDE the shot (`post.grain`, `post.vignette`, `post.focus`, `backdrop`, `environment`) instead. DISCOVERY: there is no built-in scene primitive to look up in list_catalog; the wrapper this operation registers appears afterwards as an ordinary INSTALLED component under the existing catalog rules. ASSETS: `assets` binds each slot name a layer references to a media id in the same project, and the slot's declared KIND decides what it admits — an image slot takes PNG, JPEG or WebP, a video slot MP4 or WebM. Binding the wrong kind is refused with the slot's path.

__schema127.description: A version-2 scene shot: a self-contained 3D world-object shot that scene.add / scene.update materializes into an ordinary component clip. The shot owns its layers, camera, lighting, backdrop and normalized local animation; the composition owns start, duration, ordering, cuts and transitions. Coordinates are REFERENCE PIXELS: origin at frame centre, +X right, +Y down, +Z toward the viewer. referenceSize must have the SAME aspect ratio as the composition format; mismatch fails instead of cropping. At equal aspect ratio the shot scales uniformly by outputWidth/referenceWidth. A segment's easing belongs to the keyframe it ARRIVES at; the first keyframe has no easing. Authoring limits: 32 layers, 4 devices, 16 distinct image slots, 256 keyframes per channel, 2048 keyframes per shot. Version 2 supports nested groups, procedural slab/page/phone/laptop objects, screen- and world-space text, admitted image/component/video surfaces, fixed photographic and generated studio environments, transparent/solid/linear/radial backdrops, constraints, focus, grain and vignette. Raw HTML, custom shader props, imported GLB models, arbitrary external HDR environments, skeletal animation and physics are refused with an exact field path.

assetSlot.description: Image asset slot name bound by the clip assets map; never a URL.

bakeScale.description: Optional authored scale. Preparation defaults omission to 2 and may auto-raise it to 3.

__schema198.description: Revise a scene shot in place by clip id. Send a replacement `scene` and/or `assets`; timing changes use the ordinary clip timing fields (`startTime`, `duration`, `transitionIn`). Omitted fields keep their persisted values and the MERGED result is re-validated as a whole, so a partial edit cannot leave the shot invalid. Changing only values or asset IDs updates props and bindings and REUSES the pinned source; changing the referenced SLOT SET regenerates the wrapper manifest and registers a new immutable source version atomically. Undo restores the source reference, spec, bindings and timing together. Topology, asset bindings, text content, font properties, device kind and colours are STATIC within a shot's animation — change them here (a revised spec) rather than trying to animate them. This is not a source trim or slip: a shortened or extended clip resamples the SAME normalized animation over its new duration, and trim/slip requests on generated animation are rejected rather than reinterpreted as media trims. In one batch, `scene.update` may target a shot added by an earlier `scene.add`. ASSETS: `assets` binds each slot name a layer references to a media id in the same project, and the slot's declared KIND decides what it admits — an image slot takes PNG, JPEG or WebP, a video slot MP4 or WebM. Binding the wrong kind is refused with the slot's path.

__schema206.description: Materialize a clip's SOURCE-media temporal GRID as timeline markers — the rhythm authority you cut to. `grid:"beat"` reads a MUSIC bed's beat map (get_media_context.beatGrid), `grid:"word"` the VO word onsets (wordGrid); each grid point is projected from media time to TIMELINE time through the clip's placement (startTime, trim, playbackRate, excludedRanges) and written as a `kind:"beat"|"word"` marker (`metadata.sourceClipId` set). Points outside the clip's visible window are skipped. Re-running REPLACES the prior markers from the same clip+grid (idempotent). Land cuts and transition MIDPOINTS on the markers (a 0.5s transition starts 0.25s before its marker). `maxMarkers` (default 500, ceiling 2000) — exceeding it fails loud with the count. `grid:"shot"` is not yet exposed (shot_grid_unavailable). The target must be a media clip; absent evidence fails loud (grid_unavailable) naming how to get it (declare audioRole:"music" at ingest / transcribe).

__schema211.description: Attach caption CONTENT from the media's cached transcript — no pasting words. ROUTE-MATERIALIZED like materializeGrid: the server slices the word-timed transcript to `window` (source seconds; absent = the whole media), rebases times, sentence-splits into segments, and applies it as `setCaptions`. 422 media_no_transcript when the media has no transcript or no words in the window. For your OWN word timings use setCaptions directly. For edited multi-clip timelines, use captions.fromComposition after saving the edits; that operation projects all selected track clips, trims, exclusions, and placements.

__schema215.description: Snapshot word-timed captions from the SAVED edits on one explicit enabled video or audio track. The host reads each source media transcript, projects words through clip trim, excluded ranges and placement, then replaces the caption segments. This is route-materialized to setCaptions; call it AFTER persisting clip edits and call it again when those edits change. The existing caption style and depth are preserved. Missing transcripts, unsupported clips, inconsistent clip durations, and overlapping audible clips fail loud. Playback rate scales source word times and playable duration on both audio and video tracks.

__schema218.description: Set the output format — `aspectRatio` (16:9|9:16|1:1|4:5) plus optional `fps` and `resolution`. Merges: an omitted field keeps the current value.

__schema221.description: Add an EMPTY track of a given family (video|audio|image|overlay|effect). Optional pinned `id`. The new track is appended, so it starts at the BACK: index 0 is the top layer and higher indices are further back (see `reorderTracks`). Track order is the paint order for every family: a card on a track behind a video or image track draws behind it.

__schema226.description: Remove a track AND all its clips by id.

__schema229.description: Patch a track's `name` / `enabled` by id. Track volume is retired: set each clip's own volume.

__schema233.description: Move a track from one index to another. ORDER: index 0 is the TOP layer, not the bottom — moving a backdrop to index 0 puts it in FRONT of everything and hides the composition. Higher index = further back. Track order is the paint order for every family, so cards, overlays, images and video interleave by index: a backdrop card, a screenshot and a foreground card on three tracks stack in that order. The one exception is `zPlane:"behind-subject"`, which moves the overlay inside its host clip, behind the segmented foreground.

__schema237.description: Move a clip to another SAME-family track, optionally at a new `newStartTime`.

__schema242.description: Duplicate a clip by id. Pin `newClipId` to make the copy's id deterministic (required for a clean undo/inverse).

__schema246.description: Server-authoritative: delete the [start,end] time window (seconds) and ripple every downstream clip/marker/caption earlier to close the gap. Cuts apply sequentially in TIMELINE seconds: each cut moves everything after it, so a later cut's coordinates go stale once an earlier one lands. Plan several cuts back to front (latest first), or send them as one `cutRanges`. To drop spans inside one clip, `addExcludedRange` takes SOURCE seconds and is order-independent.

__schema250.description: Server-authoritative: delete several [start,end] windows (seconds) in one atomic edit, one undo step. Every range is in timeline seconds of the composition as it is BEFORE this op, in any order; overlapping and touching ranges merge. Each must satisfy 0 <= start < end <= the timeline's end. The cuts apply back to front with exactly `cutAndRipple`'s ripple (every track, markers and derived captions move earlier), so no coordinate goes stale.

__schema254.description: Server-authoritative: shift everything at/after `time` (seconds) by `amount` seconds (+ opens a gap, − closes one).

__schema258.description: Server-authoritative: exclude a [sourceStart,sourceEnd] span (seconds) of a clip's SOURCE (an internal trim) and ripple downstream — the preferred way to drop a sub-range vs a source patch. Coordinates are SOURCE seconds, which a cut or another exclusion never shifts, so several exclusions on one clip can be sent in any order.

__schema264.description: Server-authoritative: remove a clip's previously-added excluded range by index (re-includes that span, ripples downstream).

__schema268.description: Atomically repin explicit version3 invocations using complete before/after execution references and an exact composition etag. Persistence must canonically admit scoped source hashes, destination input schemas and every resulting target context before applying, including replay/undo. Never infer a latest head, downgrade versions or accept an admitted flag.

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Get Account
tools.description: ORIENT FIRST — show THIS key's account before you spend a metered call: the org it is bound to, the current plan, a per-feature entitlements map, and per-call cost ceilings. READ `balance`, NOT `included`. CueFrame is credit-funded: rendering (entitlements.exports), generation (generate), preview stills (compose_capture), the judge (compose_verify) and the Director (compose) have NO separate per-plan allowance — they all spend one shared wallet, named in `fundedBy` (`credits`; generation is metered in provider-cost units against that wallet). Each `balance` restates that ONE wallet in that feature's own unit at `creditCost` credits per unit, so they are alternative ways to spend the same money, not four budgets. Each entitlement also carries `listUsdPerUnit`: the dollar quote for ONE unit before you call (0 = a plan grant that draws no credits, e.g. resource_import — stock search + import are free; null = not quotable up front). Check the requested cost against the balance. For generation, also check generationLimit: free accounts have a separate provider-cost cap even with a positive wallet. A billing_required error with reason free_generation_cap requires a credit-pack purchase through normal checkout. `included:false` means the plan genuinely lacks the feature. Every new org starts with a free credit grant, so an account with an empty usage history can still render, generate, preview and score. costCeilings.generateMediaUsdPerCall is the generate_media per-call USD cap. No args — identity is resolved from your key (never echoed from input).

generationLimit.description: Separate lifetime generation cap before a credit-pack purchase. Wallet balance is still shared; generation must also fit this remaining provider-cost allowance. null means unknown.

orgId.description: The org this API key is bound to — resolved server-side from the Authorization credential, NEVER from the request body/query.

displayName.description: Org/customer display name from the billing record; null when not set or unknown.

plan.description: The customer's current base plan/tier. null = unknown (billing not configured, or no active plan resolvable yet).

entitlements.description: Per-feature entitlements keyed by featureId. Covers the billing-gated capabilities: `exports` gates create_render AND generate_media output; `compose` gates compose; `brand_kits` gates create_brand_kit; `resource_import` gates import_resource (a boolean grant: `listUsdPerUnit` 0 — stock search and import cost no credits for a keyed caller); plus ai_tokens/storage/compose_verify/compose_capture/etc. Read `listUsdPerUnit` for what one unit costs before you spend it. Most capabilities are CREDIT-FUNDED — `included` is true and the real limit is `balance`, drawn from the shared wallet named in `fundedBy` (`credits` — generation included; a free org is additionally bounded by a generation cap). So read `balance`, not `included`, to decide whether you can afford a call; `included:false` means the plan genuinely lacks the feature. Check BEFORE a metered call to avoid a mid-workflow 402 billing_required (whose error `details.featureId` names the gating feature).

costCeilings.description: Discoverable per-call cost ceilings so an agent can price/right-size a request before a guaranteed 402.

billingConfigured.description: false = billing is not configured in this environment, so plan/entitlement values are best-effort and may be null (unknown), not authoritative.

surfaces.description: The browser URLs that actually exist, so an agent asked to "show me" can hand the user a real link instead of guessing one from an id. A null means the surface is not built, not that it is hidden from this key.

Answer an awaiting packet with resume(checkpointId, ...).
