tools.name: get_component_source
tools.title: Get Component Source
tools.description: Read an exact component source as complete JSON. Supply sourceVersionId from the selected catalog card to read that immutable revision, retaining sourceSnapshot with its complete versioned definition, manifest and template beside its exact pin and schema metadata. For an explicitly selected builtin, also supply builtinCollection:'native'|'curated-definitions' and its exact sourceVersionId; without builtinCollection resolution is scoped to the authenticated org. An unavailable exact pin refuses; never retry a head or another scope. To fork, keep the version-4 snapshot whole, change its componentId (the template root's data-composition-id too) and template, and send it to create_component. Builtins always require an exact collection and pin; ID-only builtin reads are refused. Declared slots are bound per placement in execution.assets, never caller params.

examples.description: Usage examples, as authored. A built-in primitive projects {name, mood?, params?, description?}; an authored component's examples are whatever it wrote, which is why the item is open. One shape for both directions: what you write here is what you read back.

metadataStatus.description: Historical source-only reads omit unavailable discovery name/description instead of borrowing current metadata.

sourceVersionId.description: Exact immutable source pin; distinct from bundle revisions.

sourceSnapshot.description: Immutable source snapshot: a version 4 template, a retired version 3 TSX module, or the historical version 2 source of a component stored before versioned sources (read-only; it never executes). source remains provenance.

tools.name: get_composition
tools.title: Get Composition
tools.description: Read a compact structural composition view by default, preserving observed ETag, authority metadata, clip timing, token values and source pins without large HTML bodies. Ordinary exact-ETag reads can omit includeDependencies. With includeDependencies=true, compact returns a dependency key/size index, not executable tokens; these tokens can contain full sources. Request explicit dependencyKeys for exact selected tokens, or response:"full" for all tokens. Selection does not establish a sufficient operation basis. Use clipIds:[id] with response:"full" for complete exact selected sources; unknown IDs are refused. Use response:"full" without clipIds for the original full backend JSON. Local response/clipIds/dependencyKeys arguments never reach the backend. READ BACK a composition as JSON — the edit itself: tracks, clips, card HTML, reframe segments, captions, markers, format. This is what create_render encodes, so it is also what you hand to validate_composition (which needs a full inline composition body), what you diff after an edit, and what you archive/share so someone else can re-render the SAME video. Read-only and free. Authoring stays op-based (apply_composition) — do not round-trip this object back as a write. A composition too large for routine model context can be read selectively with clipIds and response:"full"; the compact view explicitly identifies omitted source bodies. Defaults to the project's ACTIVE composition; pass `compositionId` to read a specific one (the same id apply_composition takes as `composition_id`, and preview_frame / create_render take as compositionId) so an A/B variant can be read back, not just written. The result includes the exact HTTP etag string; copy it to apply_composition.body.if_match (the numeric revision is not an ETag). In a compose session this reads the session's scratch, the composition its edits, previews and renders target. Pass includeDependencies="true" on a v1 guarded endpoint to read composition_id, revision and dependency tokens. With componentExecutionVersions=["3","4"], this envelope also returns expectedBrandIdentity from the persisted project authority; carry it unchanged into the matching negotiated write. Preserve those observed tokens when authoring; never refresh the basis to hide a conflict. BOTH shapes carry `needsUpgrade` when clips are stored in a retired form (unpinned or TSX component placements, removed primitives): each entry names the clipId, the kind and, when one exists, the native successor pin — move those with repin_component and rebuild the rest with create_component; such a composition will not save or render as-is. Absent when nothing needs upgrading.

componentExecutionVersions.description: The component execution versions this reader accepts, one parameter per version: 3, or 3 and 4 (native placements). Absent readers accept only the historical protocol.

includeDependencies.description: Return the immutable composition identity, project revision and shared v1 dependency expectations alongside the composition.

compositionId.description: Read a SPECIFIC composition instead of the project's active one. Omit it and the active composition is returned. Pairs with `composition_id` on the apply op: an edit you can make to a second composition is one you can read back.

session_id.description: Compose-session id: read that session's SCRATCH composition (what the session has been editing) instead of the active one. Mutually exclusive with `compositionId`. An unknown, foreign or scratch-less session is a 404, never the active composition.

clipIds.description: Read only these exact clip IDs. With response full their complete sources are returned. Unknown and duplicate IDs are refused. Omit for all clips.

response.description: MCP response view. Default compact omits repeated source bodies. Full returns the complete backend receipt or requested sources. This does not change the saved composition.

dependencyKeys.description: Select these exact existing dependency keys from includeDependencies=true. Tokens are returned byte-for-byte; unknown or duplicate keys are refused. This selection does not establish that the basis is sufficient for an operation.

anyOf.description: Verbatim backend JSON object, or an explicitly identified full selected-clip view.

Transcript and word-grid counts cover one page only (default 20 utterances); pass transcript.data.pagination.nextCursor as after to get_media_context for the next context page, or use get_transcript for exact paginated word timings.

projectId.description: Read the item through this project, for media shared into it.

audioRole.description: DECLARED audio role of this asset (audio-substrate P0): 'vo' (narration), 'music' (bed that ducks under speech), 'sfx' (one-shot hit), 'ambience' (a bed that HOLDS under VO — never ducks). Author the clip source's `audioRole` from this. Null for footage/images or an undeclared audio asset.

envelope.description: Envelope evidence (audio-substrate P0). `envelopeClass` is always present when an envelope exists (the SFX pack carries it); the numeric probe stats are present only when an audio probe has run. Null when no envelope is stored.

facts.description: Derived facts about this source (subject tracks, mattes): what has been computed, its status, and what it was billed. Same shape as GET /media/{id}/facts.

tools.name: get_media_facts
tools.title: Get Media Facts
tools.description: Read prepared subject tracks and behind-subject mattes for one media item. For an exact readiness check, pass kind + startSec + endSec together using the same SOURCE window sent to prepare_media; exact.state is pending | ready | failed | available | unavailable. If subjectTrack was prepared without intent, omit all three filters and check the whole-source subjectTrack in facts instead. Wait for the required fact to be ready before preview_frame / score_composition.

kind.description: Resolve one exact editor prerequisite. Requires startSec and endSec; the response includes the server-selected `exact` result.

startSec.description: Source-in of the clip's trim, in seconds. Must be sent WITH endSec — one without the other is a 400, never a silent whole-source default.

endSec.description: Source-out of the clip's trim, in seconds. Must be sent WITH startSec.

offers.description: What is NOT yet present and could be bought. A `matte` offer appears ONLY when the request carried `startSec`+`endSec` (the clip's SOURCE window) — a matte's price is a function of its duration, so there is no honest whole-source matte quote. `transcript` is never offered: it is produced by the ingest pipeline, not bought here.

tools.name: list_catalog
tools.title: List Catalog
tools.description: Use projection:'component-library' for the unified source-free library page, returned as complete JSON with exact scoped definition/preset/recipe cards and pagination. Choose origin:'builtin' for the maintained builtins or origin:'library' for the authenticated serving home; use libraryKind, category, q, limit and after to filter/page. Preserve each card identity.scope and identity.revision, its source/definition pin or exact recipe document identity; same names/IDs in different scopes remain distinct. Resolve the selected exact source with sourceVersionId (plus builtinCollection for an explicitly selected builtin), never a latest-head or another-home lookup. Presets identify their exact presetVersionId, definition pin and historical document witness; recipes identify their complete exact document and member source pins. This projection contains no source bodies or legacy thumbnail substitution. Omit projection for the historical catalog protocol below. DISCOVER WHAT TO BUILD WITH — list the component catalog: the one built-in primitive (heroText, the behind-subject overlay) plus your org-installed components. Desktop also includes bundled kind:'component-package' entries: these are complete reusable authored packages; insert them with the desktop apply_template tool using placement.template and explicit insert.startTime/idPrefix, media bindings and parameter values. Do not pass their ids to clip.add, get_component_source, or cueframe://component resources. Their draft status does not certify visual review or licensing. For hosted builtin preset/recipe cards, call resolve_builtin_component with the exact collection, id and revision, then apply_template with template:<builtin id> and body:{projectId,documentSha256,insert:{startTime,idPrefix},...}. Hosted tool request fields live under body; desktop tool shapes may differ. The agent-safe default page is 20 entries; use pagination.nextCursor as `after`, or narrow with category, kind, tier, useCase, mood, q, or intent. Results are recommended-tier-first when filtered. Primitive/installed entries carry the exact placement hint for apply_composition and fixedCopy warnings; use get_component_source to fork a primitive when baked copy must change. Read cueframe://component/{id} for the full primitive/installed prop schema. SCENE SHOTS ARE NOT LISTED HERE: there is no built-in scene primitive, so do not look for one — author a shot with the scene.add op (see cueframe://scene-shot). The wrapper it registers then appears here as an ordinary INSTALLED component under these same rules.

tools.name: list_render_fonts

tools.description: The fonts the RENDERER can actually draw — read this BEFORE authoring type, not after a refusal. Per family: the exact family name authoring accepts, the weight RANGES a shipped file declares (a static face has min===max; a variable face gives its axis range), the caption default weights, and whether the bytes are bundled or an aliased metric-compatible stand-in. Anything listed here passes validation by construction: it is derived from the same table the font gate refuses by. Two facts worth reading off it — every family's `styles` is ["normal"], because NO bundled family ships an italic FILE (a real italic comes only from a brand-kit font asset), and a weight outside every range is REFUSED, never synthesised. Contrast search_fonts, which searches the GOOGLE catalog and will happily return families the renderer cannot draw. `manifestVersion` identifies this exact face table; record it beside a composition to state what a font choice was validated against. Covers the bundled set only — a brand kit's sealed faces are per-org and per-render. No args, read-only, free.

Returns a fact receipt; with intent, poll get_media_facts using the same kind/window until exact.state is ready; without intent, omit all three filters and find the whole-source subjectTrack in facts until status is ready (failed is terminal). ASYNC: returns a render job; wait_job(kind="render", id=renderId) or a render.completed webhook for the URL. Meters the capture feature, never an exports credit.

tools.description: Queue durable still-frame evidence for layout/copy judgment. Returns immediately with {jobId, kind:'preview_frame', status}; then call wait_job(kind="preview_frame", id=jobId) for artifact metadata and up to four embedded frame images; fetch failures or payload limits may return fewer. Use wait_job imageIndices to read other original image artifacts from the completed job, at most four indices per call, without rendering again. Repeating the same arguments repeats the same selection. Artifact URLs alone are not observed pixels. The immutable snapshot records geometry, layers, warnings, and whether the target was persisted, inline, or session scratch. A still cannot prove motion — use preview_clip or preview_component for animation.

Needs projectId + renderId (from create_render). 422 render_not_complete while the render is still running or failed — wait_job for it first. tools.name: register_critic
tools.title: Register Critic
tools.description: Register a custom eval into the compose critic panel — the critic contract is { rubric (or rules/evaluator), referenceMediaIds?, floor }. Three tiers: rules (declarative constraints — keep-out regions, required elements, max overlays, brand colors), rubric (a text criterion scored by the judge as an extra column), or evaluator (your HTTPS webhook — CueFrame POSTs the composition+stills+facts, you return { score, critique }). referenceMediaIds (≤6 org media ids) attach YOUR reference frames as the standard — the judge scores candidates for consistency with them, so "indistinguishable from mine" is a machine check. Lane scope: rules + rubric critics run in BOTH lanes (the Director's gates AND standalone score_composition); evaluator webhooks run in the Director lane only. Use phase 'static' (the default) — 'temporal' (final-render evaluation) is accepted but not yet wired, so a temporal critic produces no verdicts today. tools.name: validate_composition
tools.title: Validate Composition
tools.description: Dry-run a full Composition object against the SAME pure, DB-free authoring guards saveComposition enforces, WITHOUT persisting it (no project needed). Checks: wire shape (Zod), primitive membership (unknown_primitive / custom_missing_sourcecode), required-param shape (invalid_primitive_params), clip↔track family (clip_source_track_mismatch), and reframe coverage (reframe_coverage_gap). Always returns ONE shape — 200 { valid, errors, quote } — for BOTH malformed wire shapes and deep-invariant failures (so branch on `valid`, not on HTTP status); errors[] lists every problem at once as a sanitized envelope { code, stage, category, retryable, message, fix } you can fix before composing/rendering. The `quote` triple states the render price to finish from a valid composition — relay it to your human BEFORE create_render. `valid:true` means save-safe EXCEPT for the three genuinely DB-bound checks that can only run at save/render, because this tool takes no project: trim-bounds (needs the media duration), image/asset-on-a-video-track (needs the media kind), and componentId resolution (needs the installed components of YOUR org — a `{kind:'component', componentId, props}` clip naming a component you have not created, or naming a CATALOG PRIMITIVE, passes here and is refused at save with `component_source_unavailable`). Pass the Composition as `body`.

kenBurns.description: Still-image motion. When unset, an image clip slowly pushes in (`in`) unless its fit is `contain` or it keyframes scale, position or rotation, so a keyframed clip renders exactly its keyframed values; set `none` for a still that holds.

audioRole.description: Mix role. A role sets the clip's default gain when it has no `volume` or `volumeDb`: vo 0 dB, sfx -6 dB, music -8 dB (-16 dB when any vo clip exists), ambience -22 dB. Set `volumeDb: 0` to keep a role and play the source at its own level.

html.description: Self-contained card markup sized to the format's pixel frame. Motion comes from frame-driven vars, never @keyframes or transition: --cf-frame, --cf-t (seconds), --cf-fps, --cf-duration, --cf-progress, --cf-ease, --cf-enter, --cf-exit. Visible copy goes in the html as plain text. Wrap a run in <span data-cf-split="words"> or "chars" and each unit becomes its own span carrying --cf-i (its index, the group carries --cf-n), so one rule staggers it (in chars, spaces count as units), e.g. opacity:clamp(0,calc(var(--cf-t)*4 - var(--cf-i)*.3),1). save_as_template binds that copy with textParams match.

tokens.description: Style values the html reads as CSS custom properties: key x becomes --cf-x, so never put dashes in a key. Use tokens for colours and sizes, not visible copy.

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

startMs.description: Word start on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

endMs.description: Word end on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

startMs.description: Word start on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

endMs.description: Word end on the composition timeline, in milliseconds.

startSec.description: Segment START in seconds, clip-relative. Segments tile the clip's duration in order.

endSec.description: Segment END in seconds, clip-relative. The span (endSec − startSec) is this segment's duration — the window `ease` ramps over.

focus.description: WHO/WHAT the camera tracks this segment (the reframe center), selected by `mode`: `frame-center` = no tracking, hold the geometric center (static/graphic footage, or a pure zoom); `point` = lock to a fixed source-normalized {x,y} (a non-moving on-screen element); `face` = track a detected face by `faceId` (from get_media_context), with optional `shotScale` close|standard|wide for tightness; `all-faces` = frame the bounding box of every detected face (group/ensemble shots); `active-speaker` = follow whoever is speaking (diarized talking-head / podcast). Pick by what the beat is about; pair with `zoom` for how tight.

intent.description: Optional editorial LABEL for diff/log readability (e.g. 'speaker-tight', 'wide-context'). Cosmetic — NOT honored by the derive math and excluded from the variant cache key.

zoom.description: How TIGHT the framing is — the fraction of the source the output viewport shows. <1 punches IN (a smaller source fraction, magnified to fill the frame); 1 = the full frame (no crop). ~0.6–0.8 is a moderate push-in, ~0.5 a tight close-up, 0.1 the maximum zoom. There is NO zoom-OUT past the full frame (max 1). Omit for the full frame. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `focus.shotScale`: a face-tracked shot is sized EITHER by the editorial scale (shotScale, calibrated to the detected face) OR by an explicit zoom — never both.

ease.description: Zoom/center ramp DURATIONS in SECONDS at this segment's edges — NOT a unitless 0–1 curve. ~0.3–0.6s reads as a snappy push; >1s reads sluggish. Keep `in` + `out` ≤ the segment's duration (endSec − startSec): the two edges share the span, so to ramp across the WHOLE segment set one edge to the full duration and the other to 0. Omit for an instant cut to this framing.

bias.description: Optional FINE framing nudge off the focus center, source-normalized in [−0.3, 0.3]. A small correction (headroom, rule-of-thirds), NOT a reframe — use `focus`/`zoom` for the actual shot. Omit (treated as 0) to sit dead-center on the focus.

__schema6.description: Ease-IN ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment START.

__schema7.description: Ease-OUT ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment END.

fontSize.description: Font size as % of composition height (1-15, default 5). NOT px.

region.description: Optional caption layout box {x,y,w,h} in normalized output-frame coordinates. Overrides position; text starts at its top edge and wraps/pages within its width and height.

letterSpacing.description: Base caption glyph spacing in pixels.

wordGapEm.description: Gap between caption runs as a multiple of base font size; default 0.35.

lineGapEm.description: Gap between caption lines as a multiple of base font size; default 0.25.

emphasisPlateReveal.description: Grow a shared emphasis plate as saved words appear while reserving its final layout width.

annotationStrokeWidth.description: Annotation stroke width in its 100×100 SVG coordinate system; default 4.

annotationTexture.description: Native annotation stroke finish; default clean.

advisories.description: Deterministic, render-free QUALITY floors (the SAME named defects the Director's in-loop verify and score_composition surface: static-hold, caption-spine, sfx-density, sfx-speech-collision, bed-coverage, audio-role). NON-blocking — they never flip `valid` (an editorially-weak composition still renders); fix them for quality, not to save. Empty when the composition is clean or the wire shape failed (they need a parsed composition).

tools.name: verify_webhook
tools.title: Verify Webhook
tools.description: Re-run ownership verification on a PENDING webhook — one whose endpoint did not echo the challenge at create time (check its verification.reason: token_not_echoed / non_2xx_<code> / unreachable / ssrf_blocked). After you fix the receiver to reply 2xx echoing data.token, call this to re-send the signed webhook.verify challenge and flip it active IN PLACE (id + secret preserved — no delete/recreate). Returns { id, status:"active"|"pending", verification? }. An already-active webhook returns active unchanged.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

status.description: active = ownership verified + receiving events; pending = challenge not echoed.

tools.name: wait_job

tools.description: Wait for a long-running job and return the resolved result — a bounded long-poll. Includes template preparation (kind="template", id=jobId), media import, render, compose, consult, suggestions and preview. If still running, call wait_job again with the same arguments; work continues server-side.

imageIndices.description: Read these 1–4 original zero-based image artifact indices from this completed job, in this order. Does not render again. Same arguments repeat the same selection; omit for the first four.

kind.description: What to wait on, including template preparation (kind="template").

id.description: kind="media": mediaItemId returned by import/generate/finalize/import_resource. kind="render": renderId. kind="compose": composeJobId. kind="consult": consultJobId. kind="suggestions": mediaItemId. Generic kinds use the jobId from the enqueue receipt.
